title: Getting Kid Ory his Muskrat Ramble royalties
summary: Learning Ory never saw royalties, Bigard traced the song from Melrose to publisher John Levy, who gave Ory a check for about $8,500, then $700 each quarter; Bigard says Ellington and Mills had tricked him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: So he did that. In the meantime Bob Crosby was playing his tune 'Muskrat Ramble' all the time, you know, and he wrote it. So I asked him one day, I says, "Hey, 'Dud,' isn't that your tune?" He said, "Yes." I said, "Are you getting any royalties?" He said, "No." I said, "Well, who published it?" He said, "Melrose." I said, "Melrose?" He said, "Yeah."
I said, 'Well, don't you ever hear from him?' He says, 'No.' 'Well, okay, we're going to see about that.' So I take him down to Vine Street where publishing row is, you know, --

-- and characters hang out. So I, nonchalant, you know, I says, 'Melrose in town?' He says, 'No.' He says, 'He's retired.' I said, 'Well, who he sold to?' He said, 'Oh, to a lot of different publishers.' So I said, 'Who handles Muskrat Ramble?' So they said, 'John Levy handles that.' I said, 'Yeah?' I said, 'Well, where is he?' They told me the floor. So I said, 'Thanks.' So I take Ory, I said, 'C'mon, let's go.' We go to the floor, the secretary or whatever greets us. So I says, 'Mr. Levy in?' She says, 'Yes.' She says, 'Who shall I tell him is calling?' No, she said first, 'Have you got an appointment?' I said, 'No. We've been trying to get one.' She says, 'Well, who shall I tell him is calling?' I said, 'Just tell him that Kid Ory is calling.' So she announced Kid Ory. He came to the door. 'Kid, I've been looking for you for years.' So I said, 'You couldn't be looking very hard. He lives out here and he's in the union book.' So he says, 'I got some money for you, royalties from Muskrat Ramble.' I said 'Yeah? It's about (unintelligible)' By the time' -- so he took Ory and he gave him a check. It was about
$8,500. Now, you know if he gave him a check for 8,500, what happened to the rest of it, you know. But that was 8,500 Ory didn't have. So --
Oh, it was around -- in the for- -- '43 or '44.
So I got that for him, and don't you know every quarter he was getting $700 for royalties?
See, when they don't know -- I mean, see, I learned from being tricked from Ellington, you know.

MR. BIGARD: Ellington and Mills, they tricked me, and so I'm going to trick somebody else and -- See, but they all -- You can't blame them. I mean, if they can get away with it, fine, you know, because that's their business.
